summary: Practise DPDP data mapping, consent controls, DPIA screening, and breach workflows. Explore the five-day compliance course and review the outline.
lede: DPDP Act compliance training helps professionals turn personal-data obligations into practical organisational workflows. It is designed for privacy, legal, compliance, technology, and HR professionals responsible for personal-data handling. Participants practise mapping data flows, designing consent records, allocating Data Fiduciary and Data Processor responsibilities, screening DPIAs, and preparing breach-response workflows.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals responsible for personal-data handling, privacy controls, or compliance decisions under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023. This course is designed for: Data Protection Officers coordinating DPDP compliance registers and escalation. Privacy Officers mapping personal-data processing and tracking consent evidence. Legal Counsel reviewing Data Fiduciary obligations and privacy notices. Compliance Analysts maintaining DPDP obligation trackers and evidence records. IT Security Managers coordinating breach triage and notification workflows. Cybersecurity Incident Responders preserving evidence for personal-data breach assessments. HR Privacy Leads managing employee-data notices, access, and retention. Consent Operations Managers maintaining consent records and withdrawal processes. DPIA Analysts screening high-risk personal-data processing and documenting controls. Senior Privacy Sponsors reporting DPDP readiness, risks, and resource needs.
prerequisites: Working familiarity with personal-data handling, privacy processes, or organisational compliance is useful. No coding or programming is required. Bring a laptop with access to Excel for template-based exercises; no specialist privacy software is required.
